root_cause_label: Broken evaluation feedback loop from persistent no-output commands prevents grounded iteration, while heuristic frequency-based shape selection omits the global maximum aligned seq_align required for feasibility, leaving plans unverified and under-optimized.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent's profiling and cost-model evaluation commands consistently produce no terminal output starting at step 12, severing the feedback loop; the agent continues blindly with heuristic shape choices that lack coverage for the maximum prompt lengths and fabricates metric values in its reasoning, never producing a verified passing plan.
t_err_evidence: Step 12: agent runs python3 -c multiline data profiling command which 'executed successfully with no output'; despite this, step 13's agent analysis text claims specific distribution values ('Bucket 1 has 24 unique seq_aligns, with most requests concentrated in 64 (134 requests) and 128 (276 requests)') that could only come from printed output that never appeared, indicating the agent misread the absent output as containing data.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16: agent writes plan files to output_data/ using hardcoded shapes [64, 128, 192, 256, 320, 384, 512, 576] derived from unverified distribution assumptions. Bucket 2 has prompts up to ~640 requiring a shape of 640, but the chosen max shape is 576, making all requests with aligned prompt > 576 infeasibly assigned. From this step forward the agent cycles through regenerate-evaluate-repeat without ever fixing the broken stdout/evaluation loop.
t_surface_evidence: Step 12 terminal output: '(command executed successfully with no output)' - the profiling command that should have printed distribution statistics produced nothing, which is the first visible signal that the feedback mechanism was broken.
trigger_explanation: The agent's python3 -c profiling command returned no visible stdout at step 12 (likely due to shell quoting/multiline issues in the agent harness), but the agent's analysis in step 13 cites specific statistics ('24 unique seq_aligns', '64: 134 requests', '128: 276 requests') as if printed output had been observed. This misreading of absent output as present data is the decisive error: it led to all subsequent shape and batching decisions being based on fabricated distributions rather than actual data.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 12, 13, 15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 28 all show '(command executed successfully with no output)' or '(command not found in terminal output)' for python3 evaluation and profiling commands. The same evaluation pattern is attempted at least 7 times (steps 19, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30) always producing no output, a clear repeated pattern of a broken feedback loop.
fabrication_evidence: Step 13 agent analysis: 'Bucket 1 has 24 unique seq_aligns, with most requests concentrated in 64 (134 requests) and 128 (276 requests)' - but the commands at steps 12 and 13 both produced no visible output. Steps 21, 23, 25, 27 similarly cite specific threshold pass/fail results ('Bucket 2 passes cost, P95 latency, and sequential thresholds but fails pad ratio by just 0.0061', 'very close', 'margin of 0.0087') without any printed metric evidence in the terminal outputs.
